entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Quiet - There was no open war, but there were private hostilities between his and Baasha's subjects.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The land had rest - Those have rest indeed, to whom God gives rest; peace indeed, to whom Christ gives peace. We find by experience, it is good to seek the Lord. While we pursue the world, we meet with nothing but vexation.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Ethiopian - Or, the Arabian, as the Hebrew word Cush is commonly used: these being much nearer to Asa than the Ethiopians.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Let not man prevail - If he prevails against us, he prevails, as it were, against thee; because thou art our God. And we rest on thee, and go forth in thy name, which thou hast encouraged us to do.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Smote - With terror, and an unaccountable consternation.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 14:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Smote the cities - because they had joined, with Zerah in this war.
